notes:
Gmail and Outlook accounts need to reconnect once (Settings > Accounts) for server filters and auto-reply.

Privacy and security
- PGP: create or import a key per account, then sign and encrypt mail. Ember learns other people's keys from their mail (Autocrypt) and shows "Encrypted" and "Signed by …" in the reader.
- App lock: unlock with Windows Hello, or Touch ID or your password on a Mac, when Ember opens and optionally after it's been idle.
- Tracker blocking (on by default) removes read-receipt pixels and tracking codes from links.
- A link whose text names a different site asks before it opens.
- Trust a whole domain's images.

Mail
- Server filters for Gmail, Outlook and custom servers, also from "Filter messages like this…" on a conversation.
- Auto-reply (out of office) for Gmail and Outlook.
- Send-as aliases, a default From address, rich-text signatures per account, and plain-text composing.
- Send is a split button with scheduled-send presets. Templates can use {first_name}, {date} and more.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Ember and Gmail-style presets, remap any action, and ? shows them all. On a Mac they show as ⌘ ⌥ ⇧, and the delete key moves mail to the trash.
- Folder favourites, auto-empty Trash and Spam, configurable snooze times, and an account: search operator.
- An account can stay out of the shared inbox.
- Junk and phishing reports reach Outlook.com, so its filters learn from them.

Invitations and calendar
- The invite bar reads the email's own invitation, shows time and place changes and cancellations, and answers iCloud and other CalDAV invitations.
- Calendar settings: week start, working hours and days, event length, reminder time and a second time zone.

Look and feel
- Spanish, French and German (Settings > General > Language), and your choice of date order and 12- or 24-hour time.
- Reading pane on the right, at the bottom or off; compact rows and text size; high contrast and reduced motion.
- Notifications: quiet hours, priority senders only, a sound per account, and what the badge counts.
- Two-finger trackpad swipes on conversations (when swipes are on).
